name: Alphabet
basis: each funding- or dividend-inclusive history is scaled to its own latest raw USD close

fundingForecast.displaySign: positive is earned by a perp long; negative is paid by a perp long

onchainSpot.preferenceBasis: all pages display separate CEX reported-volume and contract-backed DEX execution sections
onchainSpot.volumeSource: direct Binance, Bitget, Bybit, OKX, and Meteora venue APIs plus factory-verified PancakeSwap V3 pool-event volume indexed by DexScreener; DEX quote routes without indexed pool-event volume are excluded
onchainSpot.liquiditySource: direct CEX order books; direct Ethereum, Robinhood-chain, and PancakeSwap V3 quoter depth; direct Meteora pool state; and direct Jupiter executable round-trip quotes

peerMapping.justification: The block is built as an intra-TradeXYZ peer basket for GOOGL using only CORE_UNIVERSE symbols. The primary hedge is XYZ100 rather than SP500 because Alphabet's risk is concentrated in large-cap technology and AI-linked growth factors, and XYZ100 displayed 24-hour perp liquidity of 21.944 USD millions is deep enough for the hedge leg. Peer weights are positive and sum to exactly 1. The largest weights go to Microsoft, Meta Platforms, and Amazon because they best match Alphabet's combined exposure to digital advertising, cloud infrastructure, subscription and platform services, and AI investment. Apple is weighted next as a mega-cap ecosystem comparator. NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel are smaller satellite peers that capture AI compute and data-center supply-chain sensitivity without overwhelming the advertising and internet-platform core. Liquidity is respected by keeping the most economically central names at the top of the basket and limiting lower-overlap or more cyclical semiconductor names to smaller weights, with all displayed 24-hour perp liquidity figures interpreted in USD millions exactly as stated.

peers.name: Meta Platforms
peers.reason: Closest single-name economic match through digital advertising, attention platforms, and AI ranking systems; displayed liquidity is 1.343 USD millions, below GOOGL at 2.262 USD millions, so the high comparability is not pushed further.

peers.name: Microsoft
peers.reason: Microsoft is the closest listed single-name mix of cloud infrastructure, AI services, and high-margin software. Its displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is 1.386 USD millions, below GOOGL at 2.262 USD millions, so it receives the largest peer weight for comparability while still respecting the liquidity guardrail.

peers.name: Amazon
peers.reason: Amazon overlaps through AWS cloud, a growing advertising business, and a large consumer ecosystem, although retail margin structure makes it less pure than Alphabet. Its displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is only 0.462 USD millions versus GOOGL at 2.262 USD millions, so the weight stays moderate despite strong thematic overlap.

peers.name: Apple
peers.reason: Apple adds mega-cap consumer-platform and services exposure, with a strong ecosystem but less direct advertising or cloud-infrastructure overlap than the first three peers. Its displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is 1.422 USD millions, below GOOGL at 2.262 USD millions, supporting a smaller diversifying weight.

peers.name: NVIDIA
peers.reason: NVIDIA is included for AI infrastructure and accelerator exposure that increasingly drives Alphabet's cloud and data-center economics; displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is 3.384 USD millions, but business-model overlap is less direct than the advertising and cloud peers.

peers.name: Advanced Micro Devices
peers.reason: Adds a second AI accelerator and semiconductor sensitivity with displayed liquidity of 1.18 USD millions; comparability is positive but more indirect, so this is the smallest peer weight.

primary_index_hedge.name: Nasdaq-100
primary_index_hedge.reason: I use the Nasdaq-100 because it is classified as equity_index and is the closest listed index hedge for Alphabet's mega-cap technology, AI, advertising, and platform beta. Its displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is 21.944 USD millions, much deeper than GOOGL at 2.262 USD millions, making it practical as the primary hedge while the single-name peers supply the intra-market economic comparison.

peerMapping.historyMethod: daily-rebalanced peer spot total returns using the fixed Kimi weights; unavailable pre-listing peers are omitted and remaining weights renormalized once at least three peers exist; the browser rebases the basket to the target spot level at the first shared date of each selected chart range

liveSplice.method: current TradeXYZ perp mid divided by that peer's TradeXYZ close on its latest spot date; available Kimi weights renormalized and applied as a one-period return from the published peer spot endpoint; USD cash close is retained for disclosure but never mixed with a differently scaled perp contract

earningsOptions.source: consolidated listed-options chain, verified earnings calendars, and split-adjusted price history

liquidityFilter.sides: OTM puts below spot and OTM calls above spot

model.name: liquid vertical-spread risk-neutral CDF
model.description: Liquid vertical spreads are used when the chain supplies at least four valid probability points; otherwise the nearest liquid ATM straddle supplies the expiration distribution. Earnings-date log distances are time-scaled from the first post-event expiration.
model.measure: risk-neutral, not a historical or physical forecast

historicalAnalysis.eventSource: SEC earnings release history with verified calendar fallback
historicalAnalysis.method: Each current two-leg structure is translated into percentage-of-spot strikes and debit. Those same normalized strikes and today's debit percentage are replayed across prior earnings using the same calendar-day entry lead and post-event exit horizon. A profitable event requires expiration payoff greater than the original debit.
historicalAnalysis.limitation: Stock-path proxy using today's premium; historical option quotes, bid-ask execution, volatility repricing, early exercise, dividends, and transaction costs are not reconstructed.
